title: Canonical representable algebraic-space cohomology edge
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:Y\to X$ be representable. Use the actual scheme base-change functor $B_f:X_{\mathrm{et}}\to Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, its natural projection and representing pullback squares, and its abelian direct image $R_f$ [def-sfb-space-representable-abelian-direct-image]. Put $L_f$ equal to the sheafified left Kan extension, the actual left adjoint of $R_f$, and retain its adjunction and counit. This inverse image is additive and exact. Write $\mathbf Z_X,\mathbf Z_Y$ for the sheafified constant integer sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Define $a_f:\mathbf Z_X\to R_f\mathbf Z_Y$ by sheafification of the constant-presheaf unit on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ evaluated after $B_f$, and define $c_f:L_f\mathbf Z_X\to\mathbf Z_Y$ as its adjoint transpose; this canonical comparison is invertible. For an $\mathcal O_Y$-module $F$, use the specified module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $U_X,U_Y$ be the underlying additive sheaf functors followed by the canonical coefficient lift $\operatorname{ULift}:\operatorname{Ab}_u\to\operatorname{Ab}_{u+1}$. The isomorphism $e_f:U_X f_*\simeq R_f U_Y$ is the unique one whose value on every section over $V\in X_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the specified module chart-limit projection to the chart $B_f(V)=V\times_XY$, followed by $\operatorname{ULift}$. The representing square supplies that chart and its map to $V$. Define the canonical edge by the composite
$$H^q(X,U_Xf_*F)\xrightarrow{H^q(e_f)}H^q(X,R_fU_YF)\xrightarrow{L_f,\,c_f^{-1}}H^q(Y,L_fR_fU_YF)\xrightarrow{H^q(\epsilon)}H^q(Y,U_YF),\quad q\in\mathbf N.$$
Here $H^q$ is the cohomology of the additive sheaf, equivalently Ext from the constant integer sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; the canonical exact coefficient lift retains the original cohomology. The additive sheaf categories have $u+1$-small Ext groups by enough injectives. An affine morphism in the sense of [def-sfb-space-affine-quasifinite-properties] supplies the representability needed for these constructions. Neither the construction nor its normalization assumes quasi-coherence, affineness, or that a space is a terminal scheme object of its small etale site.
